title: [CRY2-8] Public broadcast channels publish `channelToken`, so an IO can map a token to a Space and
description: Review finding CRY2-8: Public broadcast channels publish `channelToken`, so an IO can map a token to a Space and channel, contrary to ARCHITECTURE §5 item 6 (lens CRY2). Location: spec/03-spaces.md:297, 311; ARCHITECTURE.md:166-169; spec/12-security.md:31, 39; spec/11-transport.md:270. Fix: The contradiction is real. 03:311 publishes the subscriber form, which carries `channelToken`, as public Space state, against ARCHITECTURE "An IO MUST NOT be able to map an admission key to a Space or channel". But a channel that anyone may read without authentication needs a token that anyone can get, and a relay operator counts as anyone. The reviewer concedes that option (b) "only moves the exposure", and option (c) adds a mechanism to protect metadata of a channel whose content is public. The only consistent fix is therefore (a): qualify ARCHITECTURE §5 item 6, 12-security.md:31 and :39, and 11-transport.md:270 to read "except the tokens of `keyAccess: public` broadcast channels, which the CO publishes". Lowered to P3: this is a wrong privacy claim about channels whose content is already public. Members' data is not exposed. Full text: notes/review2/CRY2-verified.md and notes/review2/CRY2.md.
